summary: P2 batch regression: Audit log (backend + UI) and Mailgun module are GREEN. Frontend renders /dev-os/audit-log fully with all required testids (audit-log-page, audit-stats x5 tiles, audit-search, audit-action-filter, audit-refresh, audit-table-card, audit-row-{id}, audit-toggle-{id} expands audit-meta-{id}) and DevOsHub exposes dev-os-audit-link. ProjectDetail tabs (Plan/Tasks/Proposals/Bugs/Comments/Memory/Releases) load without regression. CRITICAL BUG: the new Dev OS presence WebSocket rejects every connection with HTTP 403 (handshake refused before accept). Root cause is a schema mismatch in /app/backend/services/dev_os_presence.py — it reads user.workspace_ids (array, does NOT exist), while the users collection uses workspace_id (scalar) plus a separate db.workspace_members collection. Confirmed via direct mongo probe: the canonical pattern is used by deps.get_user. Frontend keeps retrying with exponential backoff and pollutes the console with 403s; presence-bubbles testid never mounts.

critical.issue: Every valid-token, valid-project connection is rejected with HTTP 403. presence_ws() reads `user.workspace_ids` but the schema field is `workspace_id` (scalar) on users + db.workspace_members for multi-workspace. The $in lookup therefore evaluates to {$in: []} and the project lookup returns None → websocket.close(4403) BEFORE accept → Starlette emits HTTP 403 on the upgrade. Frontend hook re-tries forever, flooding console.

integration_issues.flow: Dev OS Project Detail live presence
integration_issues.issue: WebSocket handshake fails 403 (backend bug above). presence-bubbles is NOT rendered. useDevOsPresence keeps retrying — adds noisy 403 entries to the console every few seconds. No cursor overlay possible.

action_items:
Fix /app/backend/services/dev_os_presence.py presence_ws(): resolve user's workspace memberships from db.workspace_members (and/or the scalar users.workspace_id) instead of the non-existent user.workspace_ids array. Suggested replacement around lines 150-162:

    user = await db.users.find_one({'id': user_id}, {'_id': 0, 'id': 1, 'name': 1, 'workspace_id': 1})
    if not user: await websocket.close(code=4404); return
    ws_ids = [m['workspace_id'] async for m in db.workspace_members.find({'user_id': user_id}, {'_id': 0, 'workspace_id': 1})]
    if user.get('workspace_id') and user['workspace_id'] not in ws_ids: ws_ids.append(user['workspace_id'])
    project = await db.dev_projects.find_one({'id': project_id, 'workspace_id': {'$in': ws_ids}}, {'_id': 0, 'id': 1})
    if not project: await websocket.close(code=4403); return
After the fix re-run /app/backend/tests/test_iteration59_p2batch.py — the three WS tests (happy path + 4401 + 4403) should pass. Frontend presence-bubbles should then mount on /dev-os/projects/{pid}.
critical_code_review_comments: dev_os_presence.py uses a schema that doesn't exist (`workspace_ids` array on users). The rest of the codebase uses scalar `workspace_id` + db.workspace_members. Add a unit/integration test that connects with a known-good token so this kind of schema regression is caught next iteration.

presence_ws closes the socket before calling accept() on bad-token / wrong-project / no-user paths. That's intentional but the close codes (4401/4403/4404) never reach the client — Starlette translates pre-accept close into HTTP 403 regardless. If the frontend ever needs to distinguish reasons (e.g. to stop retrying on 4403), the server must accept() first, then send a JSON error event, then close.

useDevOsPresence retries indefinitely with no max-attempts cap — once the backend bug is fixed this is fine, but consider giving up after N consecutive 4403/4404 so wrong-workspace navigations don't spin forever.
Mailgun service _configured() check is correct; send_email correctly short-circuits when env is missing. send_batch has a 1000-recipient guard. Good defensive code.

AuditLog.jsx — when entries is empty the 'Action types' stat shows -1 because of `actions.length - 1` (actions always contains the synthetic 'all' so length>=1, but for 0 entries actions=['all'] → length-1=0, OK). False alarm.

rca of the issue: REPRO: 1) POST /api/auth/demo-login → cookie set. 2) GET /api/auth/ws-token → returns short-lived JWT. 3) wss://…/api/ws/dev-os-presence/{valid_project_id}?token={token} → server replies 403 Forbidden before WS upgrade. Backend log shows `INFO: "WebSocket /api/ws/dev-os-presence/... 403" connection rejected (403 Forbidden)` for every attempt, while the legacy /api/ws/{chat_id} accepts fine with the same token. ROOT CAUSE: services/dev_os_presence.py:151-159 queries the user with projection `workspace_ids: 1` and then `db.dev_projects.find_one({'workspace_id': {'$in': user.get('workspace_ids') or []}})`. The actual users schema has scalar `workspace_id` plus a separate `workspace_members` collection — verified by reading deps.get_user (lines 93-108) and direct mongo inspection. `user.get('workspace_ids')` is therefore always None → $in: [] → no project ever matches → close(4403) → Starlette returns HTTP 403. MITIGATION: replace the lookup as shown in action_items. Also accept() before close if we ever want the client to read the close code (currently Starlette emits HTTP 403 regardless of the close code we pass).
